project: Resume Worker Sessions Through Their Exact Provider Session Reference
description: Complete ACP L4 W7 by associating every resumable Worker Session with the exact typed Provider Session reference produced by its provider attempt and resuming only through that reference after a valid Worker Session resume control. Preserve provider, kind, session, Worker Session, dispatch, attempt, and tool-call identity; reject missing, malformed, foreign, stale, or unsupported references visibly without default or fresh-session fallback; and isolate concurrent child continuations without changing projection, unrelated event, catalog, or persistence ownership.

context.customerAsk: Associate each resumable Worker Session with its exact typed Provider Session reference and resume only through that reference after a valid Factory/Worker Session resume control. Preserve provider and kind identity, stale/foreign/missing-reference failures, terminal behavior, one-session isolation, and visible failure rather than default or fresh-session fallback. Add focused tests for pause/resume of multiple children, exact reference propagation to the provider, stale/foreign rejection, no fallback, and resumed output remaining associated with the same Worker Session/tool-call identity. Do not modify provider catalog ownership, T03 projection/reconnect, unrelated Event contracts, or persistence.
context.problem: Worker Sessions already have stable identity, supervision, event topics, Runtime dispatch association, and control fan-out, while Providers can continue an exact typed Provider Session. The missing link is a Worker Sessions-owned association between one resumable execution and the exact providers.SessionRef returned by that execution. Reconstructing a reference from a session ID, current provider, or default model can lose provider-specific kind and identity, resume the wrong conversation, or produce a plausible fresh answer under the original Worker Session/tool call. Concurrent children also need isolated associations so one child's resume cannot consume another's provider context.
context.solution: Worker Sessions records a detached association containing its stable session/turn/dispatch/attempt correlation and the complete Providers-owned reference before publishing any Worker record that depends on that association. After W6 accepts a resume for a safely resumable session, Worker Sessions builds the next attempt from the same execution identity and invokes the established continuation path with that exact reference. Providers remains responsible for validating provider, kind, and provider-side existence. Any absent or rejected association produces a typed, observable Worker Session control/attempt failure, with no call to ordinary provider execution and no new session. Per-session serialization preserves terminal outcomes and isolates concurrent children.

acceptanceCriteria: Each safely resumable Worker Session has one detached association to the exact providers.SessionRef observed for its current provider attempt, retaining provider, provider-specific kind, opaque session ID, Worker Session, turn, dispatch, and attempt correlation; the association is committed before any Worker record or resumed output that depends on it is published.

After a valid W6 Factory/Worker Session resume control, the resumed attempt reaches providers.Service.Continue with the associated reference unchanged and never reaches ordinary provider execution, default-provider/model selection, or fresh-session creation.

Missing, malformed, foreign, stale, and unsupported Provider Session references produce stable typed and visible failure outcomes, start no fallback attempt, and do not falsely transition the Worker Session to running or replace its association.

A successful continuation preserves the same Worker Session and projected tool-call identity, publishes resumed output only on that session's topic, and keeps provider/kind/session correlation intact; terminal sessions retain their committed result and repeated resume is an idempotent terminal no-op.

Pausing and resuming multiple associated Factory children uses each child's own exact reference, attempts no unselected session, and cannot cross-deliver continuation input, output, lifecycle state, or terminal result when children resume or complete concurrently.

Quality gate: Typecheck, lint, focused Worker Sessions/Workers/Providers and Factory-control integration tests, deterministic race/repeat coverage for multi-child resume, and all required CI checks are terminal and passing; tests assert behavior through controlled provider edges, committed records, and explicit lifecycle outcomes rather than sleeps or meta-test inventories.

Delivery: the implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing on the exact reviewed head, every blocking PR conversation item is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file churn are reconciled against current main, and the PR is actually merged; an open, green, approved, or ready-to-merge PR is not complete.

userStories.title: Retain the exact Provider Session association
userStories.description: As an operator with a resumable Worker Session, I want its exact Provider Session identity retained with its execution correlation so a later resume cannot reconstruct or substitute provider context.
acceptanceCriteria: When a Worker attempt reports a resumable Provider Session, Worker Sessions retains a detached providers.SessionRef with the exact provider, provider-specific kind, and opaque session ID plus the owning Worker Session, turn, dispatch, and attempt correlation.

The association is committed before any Worker record that exposes or depends on that Provider Session is published; failure to validate or commit the association prevents a false resumable outcome and is reported explicitly.

Repeated observations of the same association are idempotent, while a conflicting reference for the same live attempt is rejected and cannot replace the accepted association or mutate a sibling session.
Returned snapshots and records are detached: caller mutation cannot change the registry-owned reference used by a later resume.

Successful and resumable interrupted/pause paths retain the reference when the provider supplies one; absence of a reference is represented explicitly and is never synthesized from a current provider, model, or bare session ID.
Focused behavioral tests prove association ordering, exact provider/kind/ID retention, duplicate/conflict handling, detachment, and missing-reference behavior.
Typecheck passes.
Tests pass.
userStories.notes: Implemented the Worker Sessions-owned detached exact providers.SessionRef association with Worker Session/turn/dispatch/attempt correlation. The production Factory Runtime now routes live Provider runner progress through a session-local bridge that resolves the trusted dispatch owner and commits the exact typed reference before response output is forwarded. Metadata-only compatibility values are never reconstructed into a resumable reference. Associations are validated, cloned at every boundary, idempotent for exact retries, and reject conflicts, malformed references, missing sessions, foreign attempts, and terminal no-reference writes. Controlled behavioral coverage proves association-before-output, pause/resume through the same reference, and rejection of malformed/foreign/conflicting observations without direct association setup. Verified with 100% public/internal Worker Sessions coverage, focused race and vet runs, all related service suites, and make test. make typecheck remains blocked by the pre-existing UI environment/configuration errors for missing Bun types and the TypeScript 6 baseUrl deprecation.

userStories.title: Resume one Worker Session through its exact reference
userStories.description: As an operator resuming a paused Worker Session, I want its next provider turn to continue the exact prior Provider Session so the conversation and Worker/tool-call identity remain continuous.
acceptanceCriteria: Only a W6 resume control accepted for the exact paused, safely resumable Worker Session can initiate continuation; a resume targeting another state or identity retains the established typed no-op or rejection and invokes no provider operation.

The continuation call receives the stored providers.SessionRef unchanged, including provider, kind, and ID, together with the next attempt input carrying the same Worker Session, turn, dispatch/attempt, workstation, and lineage correlation required by the existing execution path.
The resumed path invokes providers.Service.Continue and cannot route through ordinary Execute, default-provider/model resolution, or a legacy bare-session-ID reconstruction path.

Successful resumed output is published on the original Worker Session topic and remains correlated to the same Worker Session and tool-call identity; the returned reference agrees with the continued association or fails explicitly.

Resume and completion are serialized so normal completion wins with the established terminal no-op, or accepted continuation wins without duplicating terminal commitment, output delivery, or provider effects.
Focused tests observe the exact reference and correlation at a controlled provider edge and prove success, repeated resume, and resume-versus-completion outcomes.
Typecheck passes.
Tests pass.
userStories.notes: Implemented truthful pause/resume continuation for an associated Worker Session. Pause cancels only the exact admitted dispatch after a complete association exists and holds the original runtime completion path open; resume creates one continuation dispatch under the same Worker Session/turn/workstation/lineage correlation and carries the exact detached providers.SessionRef through Workers to Providers.Continue. The agent and agent-run inference paths clone and preserve the typed reference, and the runner gives it priority over the legacy bare SessionID compatibility path so ordinary Providers.Execute cannot run. Focused behavioral tests prove pause/resume ordering, exact provider/kind/ID preservation, fresh continuation-attempt identity, preserved correlation, terminal repeat no-op, and a controlled Provider edge with zero ordinary execute calls. Verified Worker Sessions/Workers and Factory Runtime suites, repeated focused race coverage, focused go vet, and make test. make typecheck remains blocked before this Go-only change by missing Bun types and TypeScript 6 baseUrl deprecation errors; make pkg-file-count remains blocked by the recorded unrelated 48 package baseline violations.

userStories.title: Fail invalid continuation without fallback
userStories.description: As an operator, I want an unusable Provider Session reference to fail visibly so the system never presents a fresh or foreign provider response as continuation of my paused Worker.
acceptanceCriteria: A paused Worker Session with no associated reference returns a stable typed missing-association failure, remains non-running, and starts neither continuation nor ordinary provider execution.

Malformed provider/kind/ID, provider mismatch, unsupported provider/session kind, provider-side stale/not-found, and provider continuation failure retain the applicable Providers typed classification in an inspectable Worker Session resume result or failure.
Every rejected case performs zero ordinary provider executions, zero default-provider/model selections, zero fresh Provider Session creations, and zero replacement association writes.

Failure is published through the existing Worker Session control/event behavior with the original Worker Session/tool-call correlation and safe diagnostics; it does not require T03 projection/reconnect changes or a new Event contract.
A terminal Worker Session remains unchanged when the same invalid resume is retried, and a failed continuation cannot overwrite an already committed terminal result.
Table-driven and controlled-edge tests cover missing, malformed, foreign, unsupported, stale, and operational-failure cases and explicitly assert the absence of fallback side effects.
Typecheck passes.
Tests pass.
userStories.notes: Added a stable missing-association resume failure and validation before a paused session can dispatch continuation. Provider-edge invalid, foreign, stale, unsupported, and operational continuation outcomes now retain their Providers-owned classification through the in-process Workers result and into safe Worker Session terminal evidence, without adding or changing Factory Event contracts. The runner always calls Continue for an exact reference and performs zero ordinary Execute calls for every rejection; rejected sessions retain their association and terminal retries are no-ops. Verified with deterministic controlled-boundary/Provider-edge tables, Agent and Agent-Run propagation coverage, focused and full Workers/Providers/Factory Runtime suites, repeated race coverage, go vet, and make test. make typecheck remains blocked by the existing missing Bun types and TypeScript 6 baseUrl deprecation; make pkg-file-count remains blocked by the documented unrelated 48 baseline violations.

userStories.title: Isolate multi-child continuation
userStories.description: As a Factory operator pausing and resuming several children, I want each child to continue only its own Provider Session so concurrent work cannot exchange context, output, or terminal state.
acceptanceCriteria: When W6 resumes multiple paused descendants of one captured Factory turn, every selected Worker Session continuation receives its own exact associated Provider Session reference, even when children share a provider or complete out of order.
A stale, missing, foreign, or unsupported reference on one child is reported for that child without substituting a sibling's reference, skipping valid siblings, or causing a fallback attempt.

Resumed output, Worker records, lifecycle results, and terminal outcomes retain the correct Worker Session, dispatch/attempt, and tool-call correlation for every child; no later turn, unrelated Factory Session, or direct Worker Session is resumed.
Duplicate Factory resume delivery is idempotent for each child and produces no duplicate continuation effects or output while preserving W6 deterministic per-child outcome ordering.

Focused integration tests cover at least two children with distinct exact references, mixed valid/invalid references, out-of-order completion, duplicate resume delivery, and cross-session/cross-turn isolation using deterministic provider-edge coordination.
Race/repeat execution reports no association, output, state, or terminal-result cross-delivery.
Typecheck passes.
Tests pass.
userStories.notes: Added a deterministic package-integration continuation proof that composes the real Factory Runtime captured-turn fan-out with the real Worker Sessions service and a controlled Workers boundary. Two paused children of one captured turn each receive their own exact Codex providers.SessionRef and retained turn correlation; a foreign continuation failure completes first while the sibling still completes with its own association and fresh dispatch. A direct Worker Session associated with another turn remains running, duplicate Factory resume returns retained no-op evidence without another provider continuation, and terminal Worker Session snapshots retain their exact dispatch/reference and safe per-child failure classification. The CI coverage remediation adds deterministic Worker Sessions public-contract and internal control-interleaving coverage, restoring both required Worker Sessions package baselines to 100.0% without relaxing policy. Verified with repeated and race execution, focused Factory Runtime/Worker Sessions/Workers suites, focused go vet, and make test. Typecheck remains blocked by the documented unrelated UI Bun/TypeScript environment configuration failures.
